title: Value Held by the Majority
statement:
In the array nums, one value appears more than half the time: strictly more than n / 2 times, where n is the length. Return that value.

The input always has such a value.

examples.why: 4 appears 3 times out of 5, which is more than half.
6 appears 4 times out of 7. The first element, 1, is not the answer.
One element out of one is a majority.

constraints: Some value appears more than n / 2 times
hints: Counting every value with a hash map works in O(n) time. Can you do it in O(1) extra space?
If you sorted the array, which index would always hold the majority value?

Pair up each majority element with a different value and cancel both. Something is always left over. Keep one candidate and a counter: same value adds one, different value subtracts one, and a counter of zero picks a new candidate.

explain.intuition:
The majority value has more copies than all other values combined. So if you cancel elements in pairs of two different values, the majority can never be wiped out: every cancellation removes at most one of its copies and at least one other element.

The voting scan does this cancelling on the fly. Hold a candidate and a count. A matching value is a vote for the candidate; a different value cancels one vote. When the count hits zero, everything seen so far has cancelled out completely, so start again with the current value. At the end, the candidate standing is the majority.
steps: For each value x: if count is 0, set candidate = x.
If x equals candidate, add one to count; otherwise subtract one.
pitfalls: Returning the value seen most often in a short prefix, or the first element. In [1, 6, 6, 6, 1, 6, 2] the first value is not the answer.
Trusting the voting result when a majority is not guaranteed. Then you need a second pass to count the candidate.
Taking the middle of the sorted array but sorting a copy you never use, or forgetting that sorting costs O(n log n).

solutions.title: Count every value
solutions.idea: Count occurrences with a hash map and return the value whose count passes n / 2.

solutions.title: Sort and take the middle
solutions.idea: A value filling more than half the array must cover the middle index once the array is sorted.

solutions.title: Voting scan
solutions.idea: Keep one candidate and a vote count. Different values cancel votes; the majority always survives the cancelling.

followups: Return every value that appears more than n / 3 times, still in O(1) space. How many candidates do you need?
The data arrives as a stream too big to store. Which of the three solutions still works?
